newsitem.title: USA: Troy, N.Y., debt seen sold as soon as Oct - MAC.
newsitem.headline: Troy, N.Y., debt seen sold as soon as Oct - MAC.

text.p: The state control board for Troy, N.Y., which on Monday announced its bondholders had agreed to waive a payment due on September 15, likely will sell debt on the city's behalf as soon as October.

"We hope to go to the debt market in early to mid-October," said Quentin Spector, the executive director for the Municipal Assistance Corp (MAC) that was set up for Troy in 1995 because the city was unable to sell its debt on its own.
Troy, which has a population of about 55,000, in July had $90 million of long-term debt outstanding and has been trying to complete its refinancing for a number of months.

The MAC official said that it expects to sell about $16 million of debt to substitute for issues now held by the state comptroller in a short-term fund, and approximately $35 million to replace lease revenue bonds issued in 1992.

Troy, which has said that its refinancing could save it $11 million, has paid a high 8.8 percent interest rate on the lease revenue bonds, due to the deal's unusual structure. The city said the three mutual funds that own the lease revenue bonds had agreed to waive a $1.4 million payment due on September 15, but added the city council still must approve the pact it negotiated with the bondholders.
Moody's Investors Service said it had put the city's single-B rating on review after Troy said it missed the September 15 payment.
The new debt that will be issued by the MAC is expected to be sold by First Albany Corp through negotiation and bear an interest rate of about six percent, Spector said.
Whether the October debt offering will include an additional part for a landfill is not yet known, he added.

The MAC official added that the debt offering still must be approved by the MAC's board, the state supervisory board, and Troy's city council. "It's always been a little dicey getting approval," Spector noted, referring to the city council.
